To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Asf1 interacts with H3 and H3.3 in a similar fashion, but that H3/H3.3 binding to Asf1 differs with respect to the residues that mediate this interaction, and that Asf1 binding to H3.3 is more favorable.

we have determined the 2.3 Å resolution structure of the histone H3/Asf1 interaction, which reveals a histone-binding site on Asf1 that is composed of both conserved residues and residues unique to the yeast Asf1 protein.

the structure of the Asf1-H3 complex reveals a histone-binding site on Asf1 that likely regulates H3 stoichiometry and that the Asf1 structure also suggests a mechanism for Asf1 to contribute to epigenetic inheritance by reading a histone H3 "barcode" to sort H3 isoforms for different deposition pathways.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of histone chaperones, the proteins responsible for the assembly, disassembly, and remodeling of the nucleosome, the basic repeating unit of chromatin.
the structure and function of the histone chaperone Asfl and its interactions with histones H3 and H4.
the molecular basis for the interaction between the histone chaperone Asfl and histone H3.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Asf1-H3 interaction is a novel and important mechanism that regulates histone stoichometry and thus epigenetic inheritance.
the structure of the yeast histones H3 and H4 chaperone interaction is important to understand the mechanism of the chaperone.

Asf1 is a histone chaperone with a conserved N-terminal domain that binds histones H3 and H4, which is required for the deposition of H3/H4 into nucleosomes, and that the structure of this interaction provides a molecular model that explains how the chaperone regulates histone stoichimetry to modulate epigentetic inheritance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the histone chaperone Asfl binds to histone H3 and H4 in a manner which sterically prevents H3-H3 interactions and thus prevents histones from being incorporated into chromatin.
Asf1 is a key player in the epigenetic inheritance of the histone code.
the structure of Asf1/H3 interaction provides a physical model for how Asf1 contributes the histone H3 barcode for sorting H3 into different histone deposition pathways.
The main takeaway from our work is that

Asf1 is a histone chaperone whose function in vivo is to bind histone H4 and H3/H4 complexes, and to regulate their interactions with other proteins in a manner that promotes proper chromatin structure.
the structure of the H3-Asf1 interface is a good example of how a protein can use a conserved structural motif to interact with a target protein in a species-specific manner.
the structure of the Asf1-H3 interaction provides a molecular basis for the role of Asf1 in the maintenance of proper chromosomal structure and epigenetic inheritance.
